extracted.intended_audience: comics professionals, creators, researchers, fans, and general readers interested in the Eisner Awards and comic-book industry awards
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the Eisner Awards' evaluation dimensions: purpose, eligibility timing, nomination/voting process, jury composition, and the full list of current and discontinued award categories used to recognize creative achievement in American comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for creative achievement in American comic books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Eisner Awards (Will Eisner Comic Industry Awards) are presented to recognize creative achievement in American comic books and are widely regarded as the most prestigious industry awards (often called the industry's equivalent of the Academy Awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Works published in the previous year are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are presented in categories for works published in the previous year (i.e., the award year recognizes work from the prior calendar/publication year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations and voting process
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are generated by a five- to six-member jury, then voted on by comic book professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A small jury produces the nominations in each category; the final winners are selected by votes from comic book professionals (the broad professional electorate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury often consists of at least one comics retailer, one librarian (since 2005), and one academic researcher, among other comic experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Wikipedia page notes typical professions represented on juries; this composition reflects an intent to include diverse industry perspectives (retail, library, scholarship, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremony and history
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eisner Awards ceremony has been held at San Diego Comic-Con every year since 1991 (with some years not awarded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical notes: first awards conferred in 1988 (for works published in 1987); no ceremony or awards in 1990 due to balloting mix-ups; named for Will Eisner; archives housed at Virginia Commonwealth University.
